backlog.spec: After the first random SLSQP solve, keep the best packing. Each later iteration perturbs the best centres with Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.02), clips to [0,1], re-runs SLSQP, repairs, and replaces the best only if the repaired sum of radii improves. Reserve a share of the time for fresh random restarts.
backlog.title: Monotonic basin hopping from incumbent

backlog.spec: From the current best packing, delete the circle with the smallest radius, sample 2000 random points, and place the circle at the point farthest from all other circles and the walls. Re-run SLSQP from this start, repair, and keep the result only if the sum of radii improves. Repeat until the time budget is used.
backlog.title: Remove and reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Pass jac to minimize for the objective (gradient -1 on radii, 0 on centres) and for the constraint function. Write the pair-distance derivatives with respect to both centres and both radii in closed form, and wall rows as unit or negative unit entries. This removes finite-difference cost so each SLSQP run gets more iterations within the same time.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include overlap constraints for pairs whose centres are closer than a threshold such as 0.35 at the start of a solve. After each SLSQP run, rebuild the neighbour list and re-solve once so pairs that moved close are constrained, then repair. This reduces the 496 pair rows to about 100 and speeds each iteration.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints

backlog.spec: Replace the four wall inequality blocks with box bounds passed to minimize: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Keep only the pair-overlap constraints and enforce the wall condition through the bounds plus a final clip. This shrinks the constraint vector and removes redundant rows.
backlog.title: Wall bounds as variable bounds

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise a smooth penalty with L-BFGS-B: minus the sum of radii plus a weight times the squared overlap and wall violations, with the weight increased over a few stages (1e2, 1e3, 1e4). Feed the result to SLSQP as the start point. This gives a well-conditioned starting configuration.
backlog.title: Soft-penalty L-BFGS warm start

backlog.spec: Solve a sequence of SLSQP problems where a shrink factor on radii is gradually relaxed from 0.9 to 1.0 across stages, so early stages push circles apart with slack and later stages maximize the true objective. Each stage starts from the previous solution. This homotopy reduces the chance of locking into a poor contact graph.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation schedule

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of gradient descent on a soft repulsion energy between centres and walls with radii fixed at a small value, to spread the centres out evenly. Then give the spread configuration with radii initialised from the nearest-neighbour distance to SLSQP.
backlog.title: Pre-relaxation by soft repulsion

backlog.spec: Instead of starting every radius at 0.05, initialise each radius at half the distance to the nearest other sampled centre, capped by the wall distance. This starts SLSQP from a nearly feasible point and reduces the number of iterations needed.
backlog.title: Radius-aware initialisation

backlog.spec: Draw initial centres with a Latin hypercube design over [0.05,0.95]^2 instead of independent uniform samples, using the seed-controlled generator. This gives more even coverage of the square across restarts and reduces clumped starts.
backlog.title: Latin hypercube centre sampling

backlog.spec: For a fraction of restarts, start from a hexagonal lattice of about 32 points inside the square, with random row offsets and small jitter, instead of uniform random points. Mix these with uniform starts so the search covers both lattice-like and disordered packings.
backlog.title: Jittered hexagonal-ish start

backlog.spec: Run many restarts with a short SLSQP budget (about 30 iterations), keep the top quarter by sum of radii, and continue only those for full iterations. This spends more CPU on promising basins and evaluates more starts in the 30 second limit.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restarts

backlog.spec: Start with a small MAX_ITER such as 50 for the first restarts and increase it geometrically as the best value stalls, up to 1000. Early cheap solves explore many basins; later expensive solves converge tightly on the best basin.
backlog.title: Adaptive maxiter across restarts

backlog.spec: Change TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9. process_time measures CPU time on one thread and the limit is 30 s, so using 27 s leaves a margin below the 45 s void threshold while giving about 12 percent more search.
backlog.title: Raise time fraction to 0.9

backlog.spec: Pass options ftol of about 1e-12 and a larger maxiter to SLSQP so that solves converge to a true local optimum rather than stopping early. Accept the extra iterations when the time budget allows.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerance

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, anneal the Gaussian perturbation sigma geometrically from 0.05 to 0.002 over the time budget. Large early moves escape local optima and small late moves refine the best configuration.
backlog.title: Decaying perturbation scale

backlog.spec: Track the acceptance rate of perturbation moves over a sliding window. Increase sigma when more than a third of moves are accepted and decrease it when fewer than a tenth are accepted. This keeps the search near a productive step size without a hand-tuned schedule.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation by acceptance

backlog.spec: Keep an elite pool of the best 5 packings. To make a child, take circles on one side of a random line from one parent and the rest from another parent, fix the count to 32, then run SLSQP. Add the child to the pool if it improves on the worst member.
backlog.title: Cut-and-splice crossover

backlog.spec: After each solve, find circles that have no active contacts (rattlers) and move each to a random location chosen as the largest empty spot. Re-solve from this configuration. Rattlers carry no weight in the sum but can block good contact graphs.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation

backlog.spec: For some restarts, generate centres for half the circles and mirror them across the vertical or horizontal midline, adding the odd circle on the axis. Optimise the full configuration. Many best known packings have approximate symmetry, so this biases the search toward those basins.
backlog.title: Symmetric start by reflection

backlog.spec: Scale the optimisation variables so centres and radii have similar magnitude, for example by optimising radii times 10 and rescaling inside the objective and constraints. This improves SLSQP conditioning because radii are roughly 0.1 while centres are roughly 0.5.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for conditioning

backlog.spec: After repair, compute the largest scale factor on all radii that keeps every pair and wall constraint satisfied in double precision, and apply it. Replace the fixed SHRINK offset with this exact scaling so that less total radius is lost to the safety margin.
backlog.title: Final exact feasibility polish

backlog.spec: Replace the global max-overlap repair loop with a pass that scales each violating pair's radii in proportion to their overlap, iterating until no pair overlaps. Keep the total unchanged where possible, so the repaired packing loses less sum of radii than the current method.
backlog.title: Better repair via pairwise scaling

backlog.spec: After the random search, pass the best packing to scipy trust-constr with the same constraints for a short time, and keep whichever packing has the larger repaired sum of radii. Trust-constr may converge where SLSQP stops on a non-smooth active set.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish of the top candidate

backlog.spec: Sample an initial radius profile from a Dirichlet or uniform distribution with a random total, rescaled to a plausible sum, and use it as the SLSQP start with random centres. Varying the size mix across restarts explores different contact graphs.
backlog.title: Random radius-profile starts

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty term proportional to the variance of the radii to the objective for early SLSQP stages, decaying to zero in the final stage. This nudges the search toward mixed-size packings early and lets the true objective decide the final shape.
backlog.title: Weight decay on radius variance

backlog.spec: During the search, enforce pair constraints with a small margin such as 1e-4 beyond the required distance, then drop the margin for the final solve. The margin keeps near-touching pairs from oscillating across the constraint boundary, which stabilises SLSQP.
backlog.title: Overlap margin regularisation

backlog.spec: Generate a batch of 20 perturbed starts from the best packing, score each by the penalty energy after a few gradient steps, and run full SLSQP only on the best 3. This spends the expensive solver on the most promising perturbations.
backlog.title: Batch scoring of perturbations

backlog.spec: Run a batch of 16 cheap coarse SLSQP solves from different seeds at once, then refine only the best two with a full run. The batch structure reduces wasted full solves on poor starts.
backlog.title: Multi-start batch of coarse solves

backlog.spec: Split the time budget into equal slices, and in each slice use a different initialisation style (uniform, lattice, Latin hypercube, perturbed best). Keep the best overall. This guards against any single initialisation style dominating across seeds.
backlog.title: Seed-stratified restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start in _solve_once with a greedy construction. Draw a fixed candidate grid of about 2000 points in [0,1]^2 using rng. Place circles one at a time: each new centre is the candidate that maximises its distance to the nearest existing centre or wall, with the distance to the boundary included and a random tie-break. Start the radii at 0.5 times that clearance. Then run the existing SLSQP and repair unchanged. Keep the random restarts, but choose a random subset of the candidates for each restart so the starts differ.
backlog.title: Greedy max-empty-circle insertion init

backlog.spec: Inside solve, for each restart, first solve a packing of n-1 circles with the same SLSQP routine (recursively or with the same budget split). Then add one circle at the largest hole, found by testing a candidate grid for the point with the largest clearance, with radius set to that clearance. Warm-start SLSQP for n circles from this configuration and then run the repair. Keep the best result over restarts. The idea is that a good n-1 structure is a strong starting point for n.
backlog.title: Grow from n-1 packing

backlog.spec: After the first restart, keep the best packing as incumbent. Each later iteration picks a random disc-shaped region with centre uniform in the square and radius about 0.3. Freeze every circle outside that region at its incumbent position and radius, and let the circles inside it move freely. Re-optimise with SLSQP, using the same scaled variables and constraints but with fixed circles removed from the decision vector. Repair and accept only if the sum of radii improves. This is a targeted large-neighbourhood move, not a full random restart.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood search on the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call in _solve_once with an augmented Lagrangian method. Use the same scaled variables. Keep multipliers for all pairwise and wall constraints, using the standard max(0, lambda/mu + g)-squared form. The inner step minimises the augmented function with scipy L-BFGS-B, which is fast and has no quadratic-programming cost. After each inner solve, update the multipliers and multiply the penalty mu by 5 until the maximum violation is below 1e-9. Then run the repair. Keep the restart loop as before.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian with L-BFGS-B inner loop

backlog.spec: Solve a sequence of unconstrained problems with a log barrier in place of the hard SLSQP constraints. For each gap g_k between two circles or between a circle and a wall, add -mu times log(g_k) to the objective, with the objective being the negative sum of radii. Start from a feasible shrunken packing and use L-BFGS-B or Newton-type steps. Reduce mu geometrically, for example by a factor of 0.2 from 1e-2 down to 1e-7, and end with a short SLSQP polish. The barrier keeps iterates strictly feasible, so the repair step rarely needs to change anything.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior continuation

backlog.spec: In each restart, sample a weight w_i uniformly from [0.5, 1.5] for every circle and optimise the weighted sum of radii, sum of w_i times r_i, with the same SLSQP constraints. This pushes the solver into different radius distributions. Then run an unweighted SLSQP polish from that solution with all weights set to 1, and repair. Keep the best unweighted result. The weights are used only for diversification and are never part of the final score.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weights for exploration

backlog.spec: For small populations, run a differential evolution search over the 2n centre coordinates with scipy's differential_evolution or a hand-written DE loop, seeded from rng. Decode each candidate by setting radii to the largest feasible values using the repair routine, and score it by the sum of radii. Use a population of about 15 times the dimension and stop after a fraction of the time budget. Then take the best candidate and run SLSQP from it to polish. Compare against the existing random restarts and keep whichever result is better.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with repair decoder

backlog.spec: Run three independent islands, each with its own rng stream derived from seed, and each holding its own best packing. Within the time budget, cycle over islands and run one restart per island per round. After every third round, copy the best packing across all islands to the island with the worst best, replacing it. This keeps diversity while passing good structure between islands. Return the global best after the repair step. Keep the time check on process_time.
backlog.title: Island model with periodic migration

backlog.spec: After SLSQP has produced centres, fix the centres and optimise radii with sequential linear programming. At each step, linearise every pairwise constraint r_i + r_j <= d_ij and every wall constraint around the current solution, then solve the LP with scipy linprog (highs) to maximise the sum of radii within a trust region of about 0.01 per radius. Accept the step if the true packing is feasible, shrink the trust region on failure, and stop when the gain is below 1e-12. Then run the repair. This gives a sharp, exactly feasible radius polish that is independent of the SLSQP tolerance.
backlog.title: Sequential linear programming on radii

backlog.spec: Add a minimum radius constraint r_i >= r_min to the SLSQP problem, with r_min starting at 0.05 and decaying linearly to 0 over the restart's SLSQP sequence. Implement this by running SLSQP several times within one restart, relaxing r_min each time and warm-starting from the previous result. The aim is to stop tiny circles from locking into poor local optima early. Finish with one unconstrained-radius SLSQP run and the repair. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower-bound radius annealing

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the pair constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 with the squared form dx^2+dy^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, and add the constraint r_i + r_j >= 0 implicitly through the existing bounds r >= 0 (keep the r >= 0 constraint). The squared form is smooth at zero distance and avoids the sqrt gradient singularity, which may make SLSQP take cleaner steps. Keep the SCALE=10 variable scaling and the rest of the solve loop unchanged, and rely on the existing _repair step for exact feasibility.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints in SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after the first minimize call, loop: restart minimize from res.x (same objective and constraints) and stop when the sum of radii improves by less than 1e-7 or after 5 passes. Restarting resets the BFGS Hessian approximation, which often lets SLSQP escape a poor step sequence when maxiter is hit before convergence. Keep the time loop in solve and the repair step unchanged. Return the final x split into centres and scaled radii as before.
backlog.title: Re-run SLSQP from its own output until stall

backlog.spec: Before the free-radius solve in _solve_once, first solve a reduced problem with one shared radius variable t: maximise t subject to pair distances >= 2t and wall distances >= t, starting from the random centres and t=INIT_RADIUS, using SLSQP with the same maxiter. Then use the resulting centres and radius vector filled with t as x0 for the full problem with per-circle radii. The equal-radius optimum gives a well-spread geometry that the free solve then refines, which is a different basin than uniform random starts reach.
backlog.title: Equal-radius max-min warm start

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres in _solve_once with a Bridson-style Poisson-disk sample in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 using the seeded rng: repeatedly propose random candidates and accept those at least a minimum distance from all accepted points, with the minimum distance set to about 0.8/sqrt(n). Stop after n points are accepted or after a fixed number of proposals, and fill any shortfall with uniform random points. Keep the radius init and the rest of the pipeline unchanged. This gives evenly spread starts without the hex-lattice rigidity of earlier attempts.
backlog.title: Poisson-disk initial centres

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw a random cap per restart from the rng, uniform on [0.08, 0.2], and add it as an upper bound on every radius variable in the SLSQP bounds (via the bounds argument or an extra inequality cap - r <= cap). Solve with the cap, then run a second SLSQP pass with the cap removed starting from that solution. The caps force different circle counts of large versus small circles across restarts, which diversifies the radius profiles without changing the objective.
backlog.title: Random per-restart radius caps in the early solve

backlog.spec: Add a helper that solves for n+1 circles with _solve_once, then deletes the circle with the smallest radius and uses the remaining centres and radii as x0 for an n-circle SLSQP solve. Use this in place of a fraction of the random restarts, about one in three, with the same time accounting. The reverse of the grow-from-n-1 idea: removing the weakest circle from a denser packing often yields a feasible and good n-circle start. Keep the repair step and the best-tracking loop unchanged, and draw the n+1 solve from the same rng.
backlog.title: Shrink-from-(n+1) start

backlog.spec: Keep track of the best packing found so far. For a fraction of the restarts, take the best centres, apply a random anisotropic scaling about (0.5,0.5) with factors drawn independently in [0.92, 1.08] for x and y from the rng, clip centres to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], and set radii to 0.8 times their best values, then run _solve_once's SLSQP from that x0 instead of the random start. The stretch perturbs the contact graph globally rather than moving a single circle, offering a different kind of basin-hopping move.
backlog.title: Anisotropic stretch kick of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In solve, generate about 20 random starts per SLSQP run. For each, run a few hundred steps of plain gradient descent on a soft energy (sum of squared overlaps of circles with radius fixed at 0.5*min spacing estimate, plus squared wall violations) using numpy only, which is cheap. Rank the starts by final energy and run the full SLSQP only on the best 2 to 3 of them. Keep the time loop and best tracking unchanged. This spends the time budget on the most promising starts rather than spreading it evenly.
backlog.title: Cheap energy prescreen of many starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, for the first SLSQP pass add a penalty term of weight 0.01 times the sum of squared distances of each centre from the square centre (0.5,0.5) to the objective, minimising the negative radius sum plus this penalty. Then run the normal objective (no penalty) from that solution. The pull packs the circles into a compact cluster first, so the free solve starts from a dense configuration that uses the square's area better. Keep the SCALE variable scaling and repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Compactness pull regulariser on the early objective

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after the first full SLSQP solve, freeze the radii at their solved values and re-run SLSQP over the centres only (radii as constants inside the constraints, with the objective dropped or set to zero), then run one final free solve over centres and radii starting from that result. The centre-only stage lets positions settle into a feasible arrangement for the current radii, and the final free solve can then grow radii that were blocked by a poor arrangement. Keep the time loop, repair, and best tracking unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-stage radius freezing then centre refinement

incumbent.description: Scale radii by a factor of 10 in the optimization variables to improve SLSQP conditioning, as radii are typically smaller than coordinates.

memo:
Helped: only slot 5, scaling radii by 10 in the SLSQP variables (conditioning). It scored -2.9385, 0.0133 better than the incumbent. It is a single run and the noise sd is about 0.0034, so replicate it first.

Did not help: a larger restart time fraction (slot 0, -2.9246), Dirichlet-like radius profiles (slot 11, -2.9361, +0.0025), and radius-aware init (slot 24, -2.9363, +0.0022). Slots 14 and 17 tied the incumbent at -2.9385 (+0.0000), so they added nothing.

Most slots failed on mechanics: patch failures (1, 2, 7, 8, 12, 15, 19, 20, 21), crashes (3, 4, 6, 9, 10, 13, 22, 23) and aborts (9, 16, 18, 19). Slots 3, 6, 9, 13 and 22 are untested on merit.

Next: spend one slot replicating slot 5. Then make small edits. Copy each SEARCH block exactly from the current file, and check array shapes (broadcasting errors recurred). Retry hex init or the remove-smallest local search in the simplest form. Avoid large rewrites.
